sections.html:
Three paths are open to a Colony owner: an agent listing, a cash offer, or an as-is deal. Prices in this city sit high next to much of Texas, which means a quick sale and a top-dollar listing can end up far apart. Compare your likely take-home from each before you commit.

This is a young city, and its earliest homes go back only to the mid-1970s. Resale houses compete with newer construction, so a dated kitchen gets measured against fresh builds down the road. A cash sale as is lets you skip the updating bill altogether.

  • Agent route: best for a polished house inside a good school zone.
  • Cash route: strongest when time, repairs or a move date are your main worries.
  • Rent out or hold: only sensible if the carrying costs work for you.

Developers planned this city along the eastern edge of Lake Lewisville. Families first arrived in October 1974, voters chose incorporation in 1977, and home rule status followed in 1979. Eastvale, a lakeside community begun in the early 1960s, folded into the city in 1987.

Age is what matters to a seller. Homes from that first building wave have decades on them, so buyers look at roofs, windows and plumbing before anything else. Sections closer to Grandscape and State Highway 121 attract another kind of buyer than the older lakeside blocks do.

The Colony had 46,196 residents in July 2025, up 3.7 percent from 2020. The 2020 density was 3,179 residents per square mile across 14.01 square miles.

Income above $114,000 and a lengthy drive to work suggest dual-income households employed across the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Anchor your price to sales on nearby streets, not to county-wide averages.

Nebraska Furniture Mart of Texas opened in spring 2015 and anchors the 433-acre Grandscape project in the State Highway 121 corridor. Topgolf, Scheels and Galaxy Theatres are part of the mix, and the city estimates six to eight million visitors a year. Trails and green space, Tree City USA and Playful City USA designations, and a spot 35 minutes from downtown Dallas and 25 minutes from DFW International Airport complete the pitch.

  • Buyers near Grandscape and SH 121 weigh traffic and walkability.
  • Buyers near the lakeshore weigh trails and park access.
  • Commuters compare the 27.1-minute average drive with other suburbs.

sections.h2: Who taxes and bills a Colony address
sections.html:
A Colony tax bill involves three offices. City council picks the city rate in September during budget season. Denton Central Appraisal District determines value and handles exemptions. The Denton County Tax Assessor/Collector sends the bill and takes payment. The levy date is October 1, applied to the value as of the previous January 1. For this year's rate, phone the city finance office or the county tax office.

  • Denton CAD: 3911 Morse St. in Denton, 940-349-3800, mailing address P.O. Box 2816, Denton, TX 76202.
  • County tax office: 940-349-3500 in Denton and 940-349-3510 at the Frisco Government Center, 5535 F.M. 423.
  • City finance office: 6053 Main Street, 972-624-3140.

A balance left after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Since the lien starts January 1 and stays with the house, the title company clears any balance from your sale money.

The city grants a homestead exemption equal to 5 percent of the property's market value, so the dollar figure shifts whenever market value does. If you receive a notice that an exemption was reduced or cancelled from the prior year, check the exemption code in the table it contains and review your status at the Denton CAD website. The notice alone does not mean a taxing unit changed its policy.

  • The statewide school exemption is $140,000, and seniors and disabled owners get extra relief.
  • Most applications are due by April 30.
  • If the seller never claimed it, a buyer moving in after January 1 may still claim the exemption for the remainder of that year.

The city exemption covers owner-occupied homes only, not rentals or investment property.

A Colony cash sale removes the pieces that most often stall a financed one. No lender appraisal means no surprise valuation gap. No loan approval means no last-minute denial. No buyer repair demands means no second round of haggling after inspection. What remains is title work, a payoff and a signing appointment.

Timing is flexible too. Some owners want to close fast, and others need a few extra weeks to find a place or finish the school year. A cash buyer can usually build either schedule into the contract. Say so up front and put the date in writing.

Start with three documents: the lender payoff, the tax bill and any owners' association papers. After that you pick a route, sign a contract and open title.

  • Order the lender payoff and search for recorded liens.
  • Pay taxes through the closing date.
  • Sign the deed before a notary, which the clerk requires.
  • Record it in Denton County, home to most of The Colony.

A statutory fee schedule sets recording charges, and your closing statement lists the exact amount. When an HOA covers your street, request its payoff or transfer letter early. A missing HOA statement is a common reason closings slip by a few days. Bring photo ID and every key, remote and gate code to the signing, and schedule your utility shutoff for the same day.

Heirs get four years from the date of death to probate a will. Other estates run on a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed. Which one applies is a question for a Texas probate attorney.

Foreclosure auctions follow a first-Tuesday schedule with 21 days' notice, so selling beforehand can keep your equity. With a tenant in place, the landlord first serves written notice to vacate, three days at minimum unless the lease sets another period. A justice court filing follows, with trial set 10 to 21 days later, and a writ of possession can come six days after final judgment. Build your sale schedule around those steps.

faqs.q: Which county is The Colony in for tax and deed purposes?
faqs.a: Denton County covers most of the city. Denton CAD sets values, and the county tax office collects, with an extra office in Frisco. Your tax bill names the county for your parcel.

faqs.q: Does The Colony have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, at 5 percent of market value. School districts add the statewide $140,000 exemption on top. File with Denton CAD by April 30.

faqs.q: Should I update my house before selling in The Colony?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Cash buyers purchase as is. If you list, weigh the cost of updates against the price difference, since buyers often compare your house with newer homes nearby.

faqs.q: How do I find The Colony's current tax rate?
faqs.a: Ask the city finance office at 972-624-3140 or the Denton County tax office at 940-349-3500. The city sets its rate each September.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I have not paid last year's property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays off the balance plus penalty and interest from your proceeds. Get a payoff figure that stays valid through the closing date.
